description: CURRENT placement offsets actually used by each component builder, for the default definition. No component currently records an explicit transform object (see docs/bible/07-atlas/125-transformations.md) — placement is implicit in workplane offsets baked directly into construction code. These values were read from the real builder functions and cross-checked against a live run.

vectors.placement: cq.Workplane("XY") with no offset; the 2D wire is drawn directly at the world origin, then revolved 360 degrees around axis (0,0,0)-(0,1,0).
Workplane chain: base offset = girdleZ - pavilionH = 14.2 - 2.6 = 11.6 (culet plane); + pavilionH (2.6) to reach the girdle plane at z=14.2; + crownH (1.4) to reach the table plane at z=15.6.
Workplane offset = base_z = band_top_z - EMBED_MM = 10.7 - 0.4 = 10.3; each prong additionally translated to (x, y) via .center(x, y) before extrusion, using the positions in coordinate-vectors.json.
Workplane offset = base_z = band_top_z - EMBED_MM = 10.3, identical to prongs (shared anchor point so the two components genuinely overlap in Z).

scalingNote: No component builder ever applies a uniform scale transform. Resizing a ring is always done by re-deriving geometry from new JDL parameter values (a fresh construction), never by scaling an existing solid — see docs/bible/07-atlas/125-transformations.md for why these are not equivalent (a uniformly-scaled comfort-fit fillet, embed depth, or stone proportion would no longer match the fixed millimeter constants those features are built from).
